free_tier.stated: The KS range is advertised from EUR 9.99 ex VAT a month: KS-B, Intel Xeon E5-1620v2 at 4 cores / 8 threads, 32 GB DDR3 ECC, 1 x 120 GB SATA SSD, 500 Mbps public bandwidth, plus a one-month installation fee. On 2026-10-22 that machine cannot be ordered in any datacenter. Nineteen of the twenty-six KS plan codes in the OVH catalogue return unavailable everywhere; the seven with stock are all either North American or Asia-Pacific: KS-4 at EUR 16.99 in Singapore, KS-3 at EUR 18.99 in Singapore and Sydney, KS-5 at EUR 17.99 in Beauharnois, Gravelines and Warsaw, KS-GAME at EUR 28.99 in Beauharnois and Sydney, and KS-A at EUR 54.99 in Singapore. The cheapest orderable Kimsufi is therefore KS-4 at EUR 16.99 in Singapore, and the vendor's own page states that the Asia-Pacific locations carry a 25 TB monthly traffic limit instead of the unlimited term the European, US and Canadian ones get.

notes: New record: the corpus holds no kimsufi or soyoustart file. Kimsufi is not a separate brand any more: kimsufi.com now redirects to eco.ovhcloud.com, and the KS SKUs sit inside the OVH eco catalogue beside the Advance and Rise ranges. The first reading of this record was wrong and the correction is the finding: querying fourteen base plan codes showed two machines with stock and I concluded the range was sold out. Querying the regional variants as well showed seven orderable codes, and the pattern is that the surviving stock is Asia-Pacific and North American while Europe is empty. So the cheapest orderable Kimsufi is EUR 16.99 in Singapore, not EUR 9.99 anywhere, and the Singapore machine is metered at 25 TB a month. A reader who wants the unlimited European term cannot buy it on this date. The catalogue returns setup fees of 0 for these SKUs while the website prints a one-month installation fee, so the setup figure here comes from the website and the disagreement is recorded rather than resolved.
